flags.title: Valuation blind-spot
flags.note: Rich valuation — P/E 38, P/B 11.1, DCF overvalued 74%. A market-beating chart doesn't make a rich entry safe; the price already discounts a lot of the good news.
flags.lesson: KPIT: strong EV/software story, valuation ignored → about −30%.

flags.title: Sector tailwind
flags.note: Information Technology is in a TAILWIND (tailwind score +0.65) — the macro backdrop supports the setup.
flags.lesson: Focus on cycles and change, not insider chatter (the author's actual edge).

flags.title: Size it — don't fall in love
flags.note: Even a clean BUY deserves a position cap and an exit plan. Concentrated conviction (loyalty to one name) is how good theses become big drawdowns.
flags.lesson: Amazon: a great company held with no diversification became the biggest single loss.

strengths.point: Capital efficiency is high - the business earns well above a normal cost of capital.
Shareholder capital is compounding at a high rate.
Return on equity has stayed high across a full decade, not just one good year.
strengths.evidence: Return on equity 10 Years 26%, 5 Years 26%, 3 Years 26%

strengths.point: Reported profit is fully backed by operating cash.
Interest cost is trivial next to operating profit.
strengths.evidence: Operating profit 1,328 Cr vs interest 63 Cr = 21.1x cover (TTM)

strengths.point: Sales compounding has been strong over five years.

The sales trend has been rising for 12 years in a row.
The reserves trend has been rising for 4 years in a row.
Leverage is modest and easily serviced.
The capex cycle has been completed - work-in-progress has been capitalised.

strengths.point: Operating profit is converting into cash almost one for one.

threats.point: A price that has outrun earnings needs the growth to catch up or it de-rates.
